classification.difficultyReason: Introduce a perpendicular to split the supplied route into two right triangles, convert the bearing and south-east direction into usable angles, then combine their horizontal lengths using the height found in part (a).

content.prompt: A mining surveyor is travelling due East and to avoid a flooded area, a detour is made by first driving from $A$ to $B$, a distance of 12 kilometres, on a bearing of $60^\circ$. From $B$ the surveyor travels south-east until re-joining the original line of travel at $C$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 18 route diagram, between the shared stem and parts (a)–(b)
spec.description: A horizontal dashed baseline joins A to C. B is above and between them. Solid AB and BC have travel arrows A to B and B to C. AB is labelled 12 km. Horizontal extensions carry eastward arrows. Filled points and italic labels identify A, B and C. Ordinary source marks are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB has length 12 and bearing 60 degrees. Coordinates are derived from B=(12 sin 60 degrees,12 cos 60 degrees); the south-east leg reaches C=(12 sin 60 degrees+12 cos 60 degrees,0). Coordinate values are construction data and are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied route and 12 km given are visible. No altitude, bearing angle, north arrow, right-angle mark or calculated distance is added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate how far north the surveyor had to travel.

answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$. The bearing gives $\angle BAD=30^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}BD&=12\sin30^\circ\\BD&=6\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
The surveyor travelled 6 km north.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By considering two different triangles, find the distance $AC$ (to the nearest tenth of a kilometre).

answer.short:
$16.4\text{ km}$

Split the route into right-angled triangles using the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$.
answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$. Then $BD=6\text{ km}$ and $\angle BAD=30^\circ$. Since $BC$ runs south-east, $\angle BCD=45^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}AD&=12\cos30^\circ\\AD&=6\sqrt3\text{ km}\\DC&=\frac{6}{\tan45^\circ}\\DC&=6\text{ km}\\AC&=AD+DC\\AC&=6\sqrt3+6\text{ km}\\AC&\approx16.4\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
